items.claim: The find-root that the adjoining span makes its whole binding device is already attested INSIDE this span at oshb:Eccl.7.24 and is never named, and the K/Q verse this row uses as its opening seam evidence is cited without its inline-ketiv disclosure.
items.evidence: A clean מצא-root sweep per attested spellings (excluding מצודים at oshb:Eccl.7.26 and מצוה at oshb:Eccl.8.5 as different roots — the contained-substring trap this book's hazard catalogue names) returns 12 verses / 17 tokens book-wide, and oshb:Eccl.7.24 carries יִמְצָאֶֽנּוּ (byte tier) inside this span, one verse before the seam this row draws. The row characterizes that verse only as carrying a paseq seg and continuing the same search vocabulary; the root is never named, so the device the next span uses to bind oshb:Eccl.7.26-Eccl.7.29 crosses this seam undisclosed on this side — and the question that token asks is precisely what the next span's chain answers, which argues continuity against the cut as drawn. The row also leaves unused the byte-true internal catchword it does have: oshb:Eccl.7.23 closes on רְחוֹקָ֥ה and oshb:Eccl.7.24 opens on רָח֖וֹק (both byte tier), stronger cohesion evidence than the tier-3 paseq it does cite. Separately, web:Eccl.7.22 is argued as this row's opening seam evidence with no disclosure that it is one of the twelve K/Q verses (single-witness) and carries the inline unpointed ketiv beside its pointed qere, את אַתָּ֖ה (byte tier) — the inline-ketiv hazard class at the exact verse the boundary is drawn against. Sound in the row: both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier, the paseq at oshb:Eccl.7.24 is in the eleven-verse inventory and is disclosed count-only, and the amarti site at oshb:Eccl.7.23 is one of 9 verses book-wide.

items.claim: The six-token find-root arithmetic and the feminine frame verb are byte-true and correctly held open, but the five perfect tokens are cited under one pointed byte form attested only three times, and the comparison to the book's other two frame intrusions misdescribes what actually varies.
items.evidence: Re-derived from the bytes, oshb:Eccl.7.27-Eccl.7.29 carry exactly 6 מצא-root tokens — מָצָ֔אתִי and לִמְצֹ֥א at oshb:Eccl.7.27, three at oshb:Eccl.7.28 (מָצָ֑אתִי, מָצָ֔אתִי, מָצָֽאתִי), one at oshb:Eccl.7.29 — so the row's count of six over three verses, five perfect plus one infinitive, is CORRECT, and 6 of the book's 17 root tokens in three verses is a genuinely distinctive density. The TIER label is not correct: the exact pointed form the row quotes, מָצָ֔אתִי, is attested at byte tier in 3 verses / 3 tokens (oshb:Eccl.7.27, oshb:Eccl.7.28, oshb:Eccl.7.29); the two others at oshb:Eccl.7.28 are מָצָ֑אתִי and מָצָֽאתִי, and at accent_stripped tier the total is still only 4 because the staged extract retains meteg. A five-token count carried under a byte-tier citation is a skeleton-tier count wearing the wrong label. Second, the feminine אָמְרָ֖ה קֹהֶ֑לֶת at oshb:Eccl.7.27 is byte-true, but 'the book's other amar-qohelet frame intrusions ... use different forms again' is not what the bytes show: oshb:Eccl.1.2 reads אָמַ֣ר קֹהֶ֔לֶת and oshb:Eccl.12.8 reads אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת — the SAME masculine perfect at both, differing only in accent. What varies at oshb:Eccl.12.8 is the NOUN, the plene definite spelling attested at that verse alone among the 7 qohelet sites. The byte record is one feminine against two identical masculines, which is a stronger fact than the row states; its own signal field records 1 of 3 correctly while the prose blurs it. Chain-start context: the root's nearest antecedent is not the participle וּמוֹצֶ֨א at oshb:Eccl.7.26 but יִמְצָאֶֽנּוּ at oshb:Eccl.7.24, inside the preceding span.
tier_citations: sweep: exact form 3 verses / 3 tokens byte, 4 tokens accent_stripped, 5 tokens skeleton over oshb:Eccl.7.27-Eccl.7.29

items.claim: The single-verse row rests entirely on a negative lexical claim against the next verse, while a byte-true דבר-family chain runs one token through each of oshb:Eccl.8.1-Eccl.8.5 across that seam, undisclosed and untested by any sweep.
items.evidence: Word-bound extraction over MT ch 8 finds one דבר-family token in each of five consecutive verses: דָּבָ֑ר (oshb:Eccl.8.1), דִּבְרַ֖ת (oshb:Eccl.8.2), בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.8.3), דְּבַר (oshb:Eccl.8.4), דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.8.5) — all byte tier. The row's assertion that its verse 'shares no content token' with web:Eccl.8.2 survives only at attested-spelling level; at root level the two verses are the head of that chain, and this book's hazard catalogue is explicit that attested-spelling sweeps and root claims return different digits, so a boundary driver stated as an absence needs the sweep that would test it. The row cites no digit, and quotes no Hebrew at all from the verse it is contrasting against. A second byte-true link crosses the same seam: oshb:Eccl.8.1 carries פָּנָ֔יו twice and oshb:Eccl.8.3 carries מִפָּנָיו֙ (byte tier); a knowing-verb thread also runs 3 verses / 4 tokens across oshb:Eccl.8.1-Eccl.8.7 (oshb:Eccl.8.1 ×1, oshb:Eccl.8.5 ×2, oshb:Eccl.8.7 ×1). None of this is disclosed, and the cross-seam cohesion rule makes an undisclosed byte-true device straddling a row's own seam argue against the row. The positive side is fine: the quoted run re-collates at byte tier, the rhetorical-question form is genuinely in the Hebrew rather than in the rendering, and the row correctly records that no refrain token is attested at this verse.
tier_citations: sweep: דבר-family 1 token in each of 5 consecutive verses, oshb:Eccl.8.1-Eccl.8.5

items.claim: The opening first-person reading depends on a verb the rendering supplies and the Hebrew does not carry, the stem contrast is asserted with the other member's Hebrew never quoted, and the only two-verse collocation of its kind in the book sits astride this row's own closing seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.8.2 opens on the bare pronoun אֲנִי֙ (byte tier) with no verb of speaking anywhere in the verse; the self-address the row asserts is present because the rendering supplies it — “I say,” (web:Eccl.8.2) — so the opener is a translation-dependent argument, not a byte-grounded one, and the curly-quoted fragment the row actually attaches to that assertion is the oath clause rather than the self-address, leaving the claim and its quoted support mismatched. The Hebrew crux here (a first-person pronoun governing an imperative with no intervening verb) is the very thing a byte-level driver would have to name; the row treats it as settled. The בהל cross-reference is substantively RIGHT but under-quoted: oshb:Eccl.8.3 reads אַל תִּבָּהֵ֤ל and the temple admonition at oshb:Eccl.5.1 = web:Eccl.5.2 reads אַל תְּבַהֵ֨ל (both byte tier), yet the row quotes only the bare consonantal root — skeleton grade, unlabeled — and asserts a niphal-against-piel contrast. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so a stem claim has to be argued from the pointed bytes on BOTH sides; one side is never shown. The crosswalk itself is handled correctly, with the explicit dual carried in the evidence list. Third, the collocation דבר רע occurs in exactly 2 verses book-wide, oshb:Eccl.8.3 and oshb:Eccl.8.5 — בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע against דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע, with רָ֑ע byte-identical at both and the head words differing only by the prefixed bet — bracketing the seam this row draws at oshb:Eccl.8.4 against oshb:Eccl.8.5, undisclosed on this side.
tier_citations: sweep: דבר רע collocation 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Eccl.8.3, oshb:Eccl.8.5)

items.claim: The row's stated binding evidence is a verbatim recurrence the bytes refute — the pointed form it says stands at both verses is attested at only one of them, at every tier.
items.evidence: The row states that the pairing recurs verbatim, and its device note states that וְעֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֔ט stands at oshb:Eccl.8.5 'and again at oshb:Eccl.8.6'. Swept from the source bytes, that form returns oshb:Eccl.8.5 ONLY — 1 verse at byte tier, 1 at accent_stripped, 1 at skeleton — because oshb:Eccl.8.6 has no waw prefix: it reads עֵ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט. The two quoted phrases differ at BOTH ends, the waw at the head and the terminal accent (zaqef qaton at oshb:Eccl.8.5 against etnachta at oshb:Eccl.8.6), so the longest byte-identical run between them breaks mid-word and 'verbatim' is false at byte tier, at accent_stripped tier, and at skeleton tier alike. What the bytes DO support is a skeleton-tier collocation recurring in exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Eccl.8.5, oshb:Eccl.8.6) — a real and sufficient cohesion signal, but a different object at a different tier from the one cited, and the row's whole reason for holding this five-verse span together is stated on the false version. Under this book's tier discipline that is the defect class where 'byte-identical/verbatim' may be asserted only per collate truth with the tier named. The row's other digits are correct: oshb:Eccl.8.5, oshb:Eccl.8.6 and oshb:Eccl.8.9 are 3 of the 8 outside-poem עת verses, the under-the-sun site at oshb:Eccl.8.9 is 1 of 27, and all three quoted runs re-collate at byte tier. One further undisclosed item at this row's opening seam: בְּדָבָ֣ר רָ֑ע at oshb:Eccl.8.3 and דָּבָ֣ר רָ֑ע at oshb:Eccl.8.5 are the only two verses in the book carrying that collocation, and they bracket it.
tier_citations: sweep: cited pointed form 1 verse (oshb:Eccl.8.5) at byte, accent_stripped AND skeleton tiers
sweep: עת ומשפט skeleton collocation 2 verses book-wide

items.claim: The hevel bracket at both ends of the span is byte-true rather than thematic, is exclusive to the span at its own two seams, and every cited digit, mark and quote checks out against the bytes and the inventories.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.8.10 closes on גַּם and oshb:Eccl.8.14 both opens on יֶשׁ הֶבֶל֮ and closes on אָמַ֕רְתִּי — all byte tier — so the bracket the row claims is in the bytes, not in the rendering. The digit is right ON THE RIGHT OBJECT — the hevel inventory distinguishes 25 bare-token verses, 30 family verses and 38 family tokens, and this row names VERSES and cites 2 of 30, avoiding the digit-blending trap. The paseq at oshb:Eccl.8.14 is in the eleven-verse inventory, disclosed count-only with single-witness wording and with the positional claim explicitly withdrawn (the checker's position warn fires on the surface wording alone). The strongest competing reading is the observation-verb adjacency at oshb:Eccl.8.9 against oshb:Eccl.8.10 — both verses open the same first-person observation frame — and the row raises it and answers it from the content of the two verses rather than waving it off. No fabricated mark class, no YHWH citation, no Aramaic label, no offset-zone ref, and every Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier.

items.claim: The one verse this row isolates carries two of the four under-the-sun tokens in its chapter and the row discloses neither, while the rows on both sides of it disclose theirs.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.8.15 carries the tachat-hashemesh refrain TWICE — תַּ֣חַת הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ and תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (byte tier) — against one token each at oshb:Eccl.8.9 and oshb:Eccl.8.17: 3 verses / 4 tokens in MT ch 8, out of 27 verses book-wide. The rows on either side each list their under-the-sun site; this row lists only the enjoyment site, so the single verse holding half the chapter's tokens of one of the book's two most widely distributed refrains (27 verses, against 30 for the hevel family) is the only one in the stretch with no disclosure. That matters here rather than being bookkeeping, because the refrain recurs two verses later at oshb:Eccl.8.17 while this row asserts a hard boundary at BOTH its edges, and disclosure symmetry for a refrain object is a sweep, not a spot fix. The row's positive evidence is sound and byte-grounded: the eat-plus-drink co-occurrence at this verse is 1 of the 5 inventory sites, the opening verb is quoted from the Hebrew rather than argued from the rendering, and the quoted run re-collates at byte tier. items.claim: The row argues its opening echo from the weaker of two available byte-tier anchors and expressly declines the digit that would settle it, and its syntactic-continuity argument turns on a word the row never quotes.
items.evidence: The opening clause of oshb:Eccl.8.16 is byte-identical with oshb:Eccl.1.17 over the run לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֔ה — a 2-verse book-wide match at byte tier, and oshb:Eccl.1.17 is another heart-applied quest report inside the same parent frame this row declares. The shorter run (the same heart-plus-infinitive pair without the wisdom noun) returns 3 verses at byte tier: oshb:Eccl.1.17, oshb:Eccl.7.25, oshb:Eccl.8.16. The row cites only the bare infinitive לָדַ֣עַת and only the oshb:Eccl.7.25 site, frames the link as joining this part's TWO quest-register passages, and states it is held without being counted into any book-wide sweep — but the sweep is available, small and clean, and would both strengthen the row and correct the two-site framing to three. Second, the rejected alternative rests on the claim that the verdict verse's own opening word grammatically continues the preceding temporal clause. That word is וְרָאִיתִי֮ (byte tier) and the row never quotes it — its own splice from that verse begins after it — so the justification for holding a two-verse unit stands as a grammatical assertion with no quoted form, in a book whose staged extract has no morphology layer to check it against. The row's other byte facts hold: oshb:Eccl.8.17 does restate the find-root three times, לִמְצוֹא֙, יִמְצָ֑א and לִמְצֹֽא (byte tier), which is 3 of the 17 tokens book-wide, and the under-the-sun site at that verse is correctly disclosed as 1 of 27.
